high.title: Big 4 Banks Raise Deposit Interest Rates
high.summary: On June 1st, BIDV significantly raised its online deposit rates, with 6-11 month terms increasing to 6.6%/year (up 1.2 percentage points) and 12-36 month terms rising to 6.8%/year (increases of 0.9-0.8 percentage points respectively). This aggressive rate hike brings BIDV's rates in line with most other Big 4 banks, with only Vietcombank maintaining slightly lower rates at 6.3%/year for 24-month terms. VietinBank offers 5.9%/year for 12-18 month terms and 6%/year for 24-36 month terms, while Agribank rates range from 4%/year for 6-11 month terms to 5.9-6%/year for longer terms. BIDV's move signals growing deposit competition pressure among state-owned banks and suggests potential upward pressure on funding costs across the banking system, which could impact lending margins and monetary transmission mechanisms.

high.title: SBV Reopens Second Money Supply Channel, Supports Banking System Liquidity
high.summary: On June 1st, the State Bank of Vietnam conducted USD/VND swap operations with credit institutions and foreign bank branches for the first time in months. The 14-day swap involved SBV buying USD spot at 23,932 VND/USD and selling USD forward at 23,944 VND/USD, with maximum volume of $1 billion. This injects approximately 23.932 trillion VND into the market on settlement date June 2nd. The 12 VND/USD spread equals roughly 1.3%/year, and combined with 14-day USD interbank rates of 3.7%/year, implies a VND funding cost around 5%/year. This reopening of the FX swap channel alongside aggressive OMO operations (46 trillion VND offered June 2nd) demonstrates SBV's commitment to maintaining adequate VND liquidity as overnight rates spiked to 11%/year, indicating funding stress in the banking system.

high.title: Overnight Interest Rates Surge to 11%, SBV Pumps VND Heavily
high.summary: VND interbank rates spiked sharply on June 1st, with overnight rates jumping 4 percentage points to 11%/year, while 2-week and 1-month rates rose 0.1-0.15 percentage points to 7.5%/year and 7.75%/year respectively. USD rates remained stable with overnight at 3.65%/year. In response, SBV aggressively supplied liquidity through OMO operations on June 2nd, offering 46 trillion VND across multiple tenors: 20 trillion VND (7-day), 12 trillion VND (35-day), and 14 trillion VND (56-day), all at 4.5%/year. Results showed 15.218 trillion VND accepted. The sharp VND rate spike indicates significant liquidity tightness in the banking system, potentially driven by month-end regulatory requirements, credit growth pressures, or FX market dynamics. SBV's aggressive response through both OMO and FX swaps demonstrates commitment to maintaining financial stability.

medium.title: SBV Loosens Credit for "Practical Real Estate Segments"
medium.summary: SBV issued guidance to 25 commercial banks adjusting credit growth calculations for prioritized real estate sectors including social housing, industrial parks, and export processing zones. From January 1-December 31, 2026, new credit growth in these three sectors will not count toward real estate credit limits when monitoring sectoral credit growth. This creates additional lending capacity for banks to finance priority real estate segments while maintaining overall real estate credit controls.

medium.title: New Regulation from July 1: Will Terminate Operations of Bank Branches and Transaction Offices
medium.summary: Article 56 of new SBV regulations, effective July 1st, grants authorities power to force closure of bank branches and transaction offices if establishment applications contained false information leading to incorrect assessment of setup conditions. The SBV Governor can close domestic branches, Department heads can close transaction offices, and regional SBV Directors can close representative offices.

medium.title: Gold Prices SJC, Gold Rings June 2: Drop 1 Million VND/Tael Across the Board
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell sharply on June 2nd morning, with SJC gold bars dropping 1 million VND/tael to 154.5-157.5 million VND/tael (buy-sell). Gold rings also declined 1 million VND/tael to similar levels. The decline follows international gold prices trading around $4,500/ounce. This represents continued pressure on domestic gold markets amid global price volatility.

medium.title: Deputy PM Nguyen Van Thang Appointed Chairman of International Financial Center Steering Committee
medium.summary: PM Le Minh Hung chaired a meeting on continued implementation of Vietnam's International Financial Center activities. The center operates under a "one center, two destinations" model with National Assembly Resolution 222/2025 and 8 government decrees providing the legal framework. Deputy PM Nguyen Van Thang was appointed to chair the steering committee, signaling high-level government commitment to developing Vietnam as a regional financial hub.
